title: Give the Meeting a Facilitator: draft 2 as a string with Onboard, Don't Program - 19 changes (can wait to Monday)
summary:
Draft 2: Onboard, Don't Program -> Give the Meeting a Facilitator. Your brainstorm is now a before / during / after menu; you build your own facilitator through the five parts and a playback, mark each job "alone" or "ask", and hand it the briefing at the start of every meeting. Kept: note taking is not enough; the ask-the-host etiquette; Teams as one line. Governance, Practice. Value names a meeting coordinator or administrative assistant with no pay figure (none verified yet).

Your confirmed team: Rachel Kim, Tony Alvarez, Denise Holloway, Victor Lindqvist (adversarial). Changes 12 and 18 come at the same menu item from opposite sides. Voices: https://github.com/level5consulting/ai-success-patterns/blob/overnight-2026-11-12/records/red-team-29-facilitator-draft2.md

Monday night builds draft 3 and its In Review page, so this one can wait to Monday morning.

questions.text: Change 1: Ask "who are you and which meetings do you run" before showing the menu, so jobs are picked per meeting type (Rachel Kim)
Change 2: Say plainly whether it's one briefing per recurring meeting or one briefing with a section per meeting type (Rachel Kim)
Change 3: Say, tool-neutrally, how to make the standing briefing stick (a saved project, custom instructions, a pinned document) so only the meeting's goal is added each time (Rachel Kim)
Change 4: Add a "start here" trio - agenda from the record, time reminders, draft notes for a person to check (Rachel Kim)
Change 5: Use time zones (a "day before" reminder landing at three different times) as the example of a gap the playback catches (Rachel Kim)
Change 6: In Step 3, say "alone" can never be more than your organization and your license allow - check what the tool can reach first (Tony Alvarez)
Change 7: Add retention: where recordings, transcripts and notes are kept and for how long follows your organization's rules (Tony Alvarez)
Change 8: Change "any AI can work from a transcript" to a tool your organization approved for meeting content, and add Avoid the Naughty List to the string (Tony Alvarez)
Change 9: A briefing with "alone" jobs that send anything gets a second look from the meeting owner or whoever governs AI use (Tony Alvarez)
Change 10: Add to the menu: confirm the room or link works; check the people needed for the decision accepted; reschedule when the key person declines (Denise Holloway)
Change 11: Name the pre-meeting heads-up with the leader (who's upset, what she's walking into) as a people job, not a menu item (Denise Holloway)
Change 12: "Who hasn't spoken" goes to the chair privately, never out loud in the room (Denise Holloway)
Change 13: Add relationships to "What stays with people": who gets a heads-up before a decision lands, who hears bad news in person (Denise Holloway)
Change 14: Use "who is the nudge from?" as the alone/ask example (Denise Holloway)
Change 15: Make "Should this meeting exist?" the first job on the menu (Victor Lindqvist, adversarial)
Change 16: Have the facilitator flag at the start when a meeting has no decision on its agenda (Victor Lindqvist)
Change 17: Add total meeting hours to Measure it - if prep hours fall and meeting hours rise, the pattern has failed (Victor Lindqvist)
Change 18: Drop "tell the chair who hasn't spoken" as surveillance - or keep it with the judgment with the chair and the count never in the notes (Victor Lindqvist)
Change 19: Add a line that the goal is fewer, better meetings - not the same meetings with less effort (Victor Lindqvist)
When?
questions.detail: Later: say when in the note.
